formula: V(L) = V(L_b) * (1 + g_band)^(L - L_b), continuous at band edges

tiers.name: Pilgrim
tiers.Design_Intent: Onboarding. Enemies die well inside the 15-turn window to any legal swap; tests only that the player understands swapping, colour→mana and that skulls are the threat. Ailments are rare enough to be read as a tutorial event.

tiers.name: Wanderer
tiers.Design_Intent: Line shape. Rewards making 4-in-a-row for the extra turn over the first match seen; a player who never chains still wins, one who does wins in about half the turns.

tiers.name: Apprentice
tiers.Design_Intent: Skull triage. Skull damage reaches 1x, so the test is denying enemy skull matches (clearing skull lines before they fall to the enemy) rather than pure damage racing.

tiers.name: Journeyman
tiers.Design_Intent: First skill rotation. HP outgrows raw matching; the player must spend mana on a skill every few turns instead of hoarding, and first sees enrage as a real deadline on bosses.

tiers.name: Adept
tiers.Design_Intent: Normal baseline (≈ the current Normal row). Boss tactics on every third enemy turn now cost real HP; tests reading the board after a reshape and planning potions for guardians.

tiers.name: Tactician
tiers.Design_Intent: Cascade awareness. The kill window shrinks while HP compounds at 18%/tier: the player must favour low-board matches that drop new lines (combo multiplier) over top-board safe moves.

tiers.name: Strategist
tiers.Design_Intent: Ailment management. ~15% of Elite/Boss actions carry Burning/Poison/Freeze; tests cleansing or out-racing damage-over-time and not wasting a frozen turn window.

tiers.name: Veteran
tiers.Design_Intent: Mana efficiency (past Hard: ~1.5x HP and skulls). Every skill cast must be timed to a full board state; tests banking mana toward one burst into an enemy vulnerability rather than casting on cooldown.

tiers.name: Warden
tiers.Design_Intent: Gear & research check. Raw HP at ~1.8x with 12 turns to enrage means un-upgraded gear fails mathematically; tests whether the player has invested in forge and research instead of pushing.

tiers.name: Champion
tiers.Design_Intent: Optimized ceiling (above Grindmaster: ~2.2x HP, ~1.9x skulls). Requires a deliberate opener: set up a 4+/Catalyst on turn 1–3, sustain combos ≥3 on average, and finish before enrage at 12.

tiers.name: Scourge
tiers.Design_Intent: Mega-combo entry. HP growth jumps to 30%/tier; average play no longer clears before enrage. Tests engineering cascades ≥5 and chaining extra turns, not finding them by luck.

tiers.name: Torment
tiers.Design_Intent: Enrage is assumed. The window (~10 turns) is shorter than a clean kill for most builds; tests surviving post-enrage skulls ×2 + scorch with shields, cleanses and heal timing.

tiers.name: Abyssal
tiers.Design_Intent: Status saturation. Over half of Elite/Boss actions inflict an ailment; tests build choice (resistances, cleanse skills) as much as board play — the wrong loadout cannot win.

tiers.name: Oblivion
tiers.Design_Intent: Near-perfect execution. 8 turns to enrage, ~6.2x HP, 4x skulls and ~64% ailments; every turn must either set up or cash in a mega-combo. One wasted move is usually the fight.

tiers.name: Endless Grind
tiers.Design_Intent: Masochist ceiling. Enrage at the 8-turn floor, ~8x HP, ~4.8x skulls, ailments at the 0.75 cap, rewards at the 0.4x floor: solvable only with a min-maxed build plus Catalyst wipes and long cascades. A prestige tier, not a farming tier.
